text:
marta: heads-up — seeing a weird pattern in us-west2: warm pool GPUs show ~40% idle but a lot of tiny pod jobs are pending. they _don't_ binpack onto warm nodes, instead go to normal nodes and get evicted/backs off.
alex: any recent scheduler or warm-pool changes?
marta: nothing on scheduler in prod, autoscaler had a minor config tweak last week. this popped up after a short API throttling window.
sre-bot: alert: PendingPods>100 in cluster/us-west2-gpu at 2026-03-19T14:02Z :warning: 
jin: can you paste a failing pod's spec and the node labels? my first guess is affinity/taint mismatch but you said labels are present.
marta: example pod snippet: `nodeSelector: {gpu: "true", size: "small"}` — warm nodes have `pool: warm` and `gpu: true`. labels are there. scheduler logs show lots of "no suitable node found" entries for these tiny pods even though warm nodes are free.

alex: paste scheduler log lines around the errors?
marta: ```
I0329 14:01:58.123 scheduler.go:512] FailedFit Pod default/job-xyz: no matching node; predicate: NodeSelector
I0329 14:01:58.124 scheduler.go:634] Score warmpool-node-7: 10
I0329 14:01:58.124 scheduler.go:634] Score normal-node-21: 95
```
jin: that scoring skew looks suspicious — warmpool scoring low. check NodeConditions / allocatable reported by kubelet on warm nodes (maybe resource view is stale).
marta: `kubectl get nodes -l pool=warm -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name} {.status.allocatable} {.status.conditions[-1].lastHeartbeatTime}\n'` shows allocatable gpu=1 but lastHeartbeatTime is older than usual for several warm nodes (api-server throttled around 14:00).
ryan: could be informer cache staleness in scheduler. we saw this pattern before when resyncPeriod and apiserver latency interact — scheduler continues to make decisions against slightly outdated node status so it prefers non-warm nodes.
alex: do we have a metric for informer lag / resourceVersion errors? where to look?
jin: infra.sched.informer_lag and infra.k8s.resource_version_retries. dashboards spiked at ~14:00 matching the API throttle.
marta: confirmed. informer_lag jumped and the scheduler emitted several "skipping node(s) due to stale snapshot" warnings.

alex: mitigation options? prefer least-risky first.
jin: 1) non-invasive: add a soft affinity rule for tiny pods (label tiny=true) and add a preferredAffinity on warm nodes to match tiny=true. That will bias scheduler toward warm nodes without touching scheduler internals.
jin: 2) operational: force a scheduler cache refresh (rolling restart of kube-scheduler primaries) to drop the stale view. 3) short-term: adjust warm-pool tolerations/taints to accept tiny pods explicitly.
ryan: I prefer 1 then 2. restarting scheduler during a small window is fine but invasive; affinity change is safer and reversible. Also add alerting for informer_lag thresholds.

marta: I'll rollout option 1 now: patch the job templates to include label `tiny=true` for small workloads and annotate warm nodes with a preferredAffinity rule. creating a ticket INFRA-4521 to track this.
alex: please also capture the exact scheduler log lines / resourceVersion mismatch for the ticket.
marta: pasted log excerpt to the ticket and linked the informer_lag dashboard. applying the label change to the job-generator in CI now.
sre-bot: deploybot: hotfix queued: job-generator svc revision 2026.03.19-7 (rolling) :white_check_mark: 
jin: after hotfix, monitor pending pods count and eviction rates. if no improvement, plan for a scheduler restart during the maintenance window. Also audit kubelet versions — older kubelets sometimes report conditions in slightly different fields which confuses scoring plugins.
ryan: adding kubelet version matrix and node heartbeat histogram to INFRA-4521.
alex: assign owners and target for full fix (resync tuning + observability).
marta: owners: marta, jin, ryan. target: maintenance window 2026-03-22. mitigation applied now. will post metrics after 1hr. :rocket: 

ryan: rollback plan?
marta: revert job-label change and scale warm pool down-to-zero if it regresses. documented in the ticket.
alex: thanks. keep updates here. :thumbsup:
marta: will do — initial numbers look promising (pending down 60% after the label patch). posting dashboard link in 20m.
sre-bot: note: incident-saver archived alert id 98765 to INFRA-4521.
